dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: Welcome to Morepesok! If there is anything you need, please don't hesitate to let me know.

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: I'm in charge of the Snezhnayan Line here at Morepesok. If you have any questions about the trains passing through, just ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: Honestly, nobody knows the ins and outs of this station better than me. I've been serving here for almost a decade.

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: There's actually quite a lot to do around Morepesok. You can try ice fishing, go for a sled ride, or grab some barbecue at Razumovsky's stall!

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: If you ask me, his barbecue sauce is nothing special, but at least the fish and meat are always fresh.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's all the questions I have for now...

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: Alright. May you have a pleasant journey.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is working at the Transport Bureau really that stable?

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: It's less about stability, and more that... I don't really have a choice...

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: Back when I was young, I worked at the Snezhnograd Central Station. I made a severe scheduling oversight that led to a terrible accident. They shipped me off to Morepesok right after.

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: Honestly, I fell into a pretty dark place for a while, but I've come to terms with it now. No matter where you land, you've got to take pride in your work and do a proper job.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're a real veteran around here!

dialogues.speaker: Znamensky
dialogues.text: Yeah. So if there's anything you want to know, don't hesitate to come find me.
